cohort: 9,121 late preterm infants (LPI) enrolled from 34 hospitals in the SEN34-36 database over a five year period.
finding: Late preterm infants (LPIs) had significantly higher rates of morbidity and mortality compared to term babies, highlighting the need for revised obstetric protocols and specialized perinatal care for this at-risk population.
mod_finding: The study found a cesarean section rate of 47.9% in the LPI group, with 44.4% being planned and 18.8% having no justified reason.
